News.title: Wu Yize beats Shaun Murphy in classic final – with help from a crafty cigarette
News.content:
A World Championship that virtually had it all received the extraordinary finale it deserved. A final-frame decider, the first in 24 years, between Shaun Murphy and Wu Yize, ended with the 22-year-old from China finally emerging victorious at Sheffield’s Crucible Theatre.

After a scintillating climax which matched that 2002 epic, where Peter Ebdon triumphed over Stephen Hendry, Wu became the second-youngest winner of this iconic tournament and also the second Chinese winner after Zhao Xintong last year. Wu is a prodigious talent who took the Crucible by storm, sealing the championship with the coolest of left-handed pots.

Lanzhou-born Wu moved to Sheffield with his father when he was 16 to pursue his snooker dream in what must surely rank as one of the game’s most remarkable rags-to-riches tales. The duo shared a window-less flat and even a bed in Sheffield but, as Wu pumped his fist after conquering 43-year-old Murphy in this epic, all of that hardship was worth it.

In the Steel City, Wu’s nerves matched. He has developed into a cult figure with the Crucible faithful and his Wu Fan Clan were there until the very end, chanting his surname in the same vein as fans of Joe Root or Bruce Springsteen after a final for the ages.

“My parents are the true champions,” said an emotional Wu. “They are the source of my strengths. I love them so much. I am so happy. I played for myself, my family, and China. I think other Chinese players can win this championship – the best is yet to come.”

News.title: Chelsea humiliated by second-string Nottingham Forest to crush Champions League hopes
News.content:
Both sides want and need a win, but for very different reasons.

Chelsea have lost five Premier League matches in a row for the first time since 1993, they are without a manager and to top it all off, haven’t scored during those five sorry defeats, some thing that hasn’t happened since 1912. In short, the club is in trouble and not in the usual Stamford Bridge sense of crisis, they are in actual real disarray.

Today’s hosts lie in ninth, four points off Bournemouth in sixth and in danger of not securing European football next season.

Their opponents come into today’s match in contrasting form. Nottingham Forest are unbeaten in their past six league matches and have scored nine goals in their past two as they try and secure their top-flight safety.

Their 5-0 win against Sunderland secured back-to-back Premier League wins for only the second time this season, and for the first time under Vitor Pereira. Another today at Stamford Bridge would mean a third in a row for the first time last season and go a long way to ensuring they remain in the top flight for another campaign.

The good news for Chelsea is that Cole Palmer could make his first start since a minor hamstring setback left him on the sidelines.

“It has been a difficult period for him,” interim Chelsea manager Calum McFarlane said. “It is the first injury he has pretty much ever had in his career.

“There are obviously games he can impact more, but there have also been plenty of occasions where he has created good chances for others. He can’t control whether those chances are finished - he can only put the ball where it needs to be.

“He’s had some really good games over the past three months. It is just a case of building consistency, so overall I’m really pleased with him.

“He is still a top, top player - one of the best in the world. I’ve got no concerns about him being ready to impact games from now until the end of the season, and hopefully in the World Cup in the big moments for England.”

Stay here for all the team news and action, with kick-off set for 3pm.

News.title: De Zerbi has Spurs believing again as Villa win moves them out of drop zone
News.content:
Spurs were prepared to stump up the £34m fee demanded by Atlético Madrid. Villa proposed a loan with an option to buy which will have frustrated Unai Emery. But not as much as this shocking performance even if, in truth, Spurs have had a poor return from Gallagher up until now.

Having declared last week that “only losers cry”, doubling down on his belief that Spurs will survive then this was the perfect reaction for De Zerbi. It also showed that Spurs have the “big manager” they craved and how they have lucked out in hiring the Italian.

“He makes you feel so good. He brings the best out of you,” Gallagher said. It felt like a universal belief and that might just be enough.

“I am honest. I have one face. If I say all our players are great level it’s because I feel. I don’t want to sell something if I don’t believe in my words,” De Zerbi said. “My job is just to transfer the confidence and believe in themselves. To show passion, to show value, pride.”

He grabbed his shirt just as Palhinha had done. “I love Palhinha,” he added, declaring that this version of Gallagher was like having “12 players”.

Okay, Villa’s Emery made seven changes ahead of Thursday’s momentous Europa League semi-final second leg at home to Nottingham Forest.

But after Spurs scored their second goal there were boos and an exodus of fans to the concourses – and maybe the exits. Just 25 minutes had elapsed. And it could have been four.

That crowd reaction – and there was more – must have provoked a maelstrom of emotions for Emery at a club where he rules the roost and has Messiah-status. On the touchline his demeanour radiated the definition of “if looks could kill”.

For Spurs, De Zerbi may be conferred similar God-like status if he keeps them up. With three games to go, albeit three demanding fixtures, they are a point ahead of West Ham United who have replaced them in the bottom three. It is that tight. But they are up for the fight.

News.title: Snooker on brink of seismic change as Wu surges into 10-7 World Championship final lead
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the World Snooker Championship, as Shaun Murphy takes on Wu Yize.

Yize battled past Mark Allen in his semi-final, with the Englishman missing a match-winning black before Yize claimed a 17-16 victory.

The match-up will be best remembered for a 14th frame that lasted for more than 100 minutes, so we can be sure that at the very least, Yize possesses the necessary stamina for this best-of-35 tie.

For Murphy, Yize is his fourth Chinese opponent in the tournament, having already beaten Fan Zhengyi, Xiao Guodong and Zhao Xintong. His semi-final tie was against John Higgins, as Murphy won 17-15.

Murphy is in decent form this season. He is the 2025 Masters champion, and won the British Open earlier this year. He also was the losing finalist at the Xi’an Grand Prix and the German Masters.

Yize, just 22, also has a 2026 title to his name after lifting the International Championship title, and was beaten in the final of the Championship League earlier in the year.

The youngster is ranked No. 10 in the world, while Murphy is the No. 8 in the standings. At 43, Murphy boasts two decades of experience on his opponent, and rarely appears short of confidence when it comes to his own abilities.

That single-mindedness will be examined under pressure in the Crucible Theatre over the coming two days,

In 2005, Murphy became just the third qualifier to win the World Championship, and he has since lost three finals in the tournament, in 2009, 2015 and 2021. He is the favourite to claim his second win on this Bank Holiday weekend, but Yize’s own undeniable quality makes him a strong contender too.

There are two sessions scheduled for today, and two more for Monday.

Sports.title: Declan Rice jumps into Arsenal fans as ‘chaos’ celebrations erupt in dressing room and fans have boozy party in streets
Sports.content:
DELIGHTED Declan Rice jumped into the jubilant Arsenal fans – before dancing in the “chaotic” dressing room celebrations.

And Arsenal booking their place in the Champions League final for the first time since 2006 sparked boozy partying in the streets, too.





Bukayo Saka scored the only goal of the game to settle the semi-final second leg against Atletico Madrid at the Emirates.

After a 1-1 draw in Spain last week, the winger reacted fastest to turn in the rebound from Leandro Trossard’s shot.

And when the full-time whistle blew – moments after tensions boiled over on the touchline – the Emirates erupted.

The players and coaching staff enjoyed a lap of honour, soaking up the incredible atmosphere and relentless singing.

Rice, who was phenomenal throughout the game, then showed his appreciation for the Arsenal supporters.

The midfielder jumped over the advertising hoardings and ran towards the front row of the stand, yelling and hugging the fans.

They responded by clutching the £105million signing and slapping him on the back in a brilliant moment.

Rice, 27, then told Prime Video that the scenes were even more wild behind closed doors.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Asked about the dressing room, he said: “It is chaos.

“I don’t think you can underestimate what we have done in this competition up to this point.

“I think we have every right to celebrate that moment. The most prestigious competition in club football. We are just trying to soak it all in.

“We knew coming into the game what was at stake.

“If you can’t get up for that, then you can’t get up for any game of football.



“When we went 1-0 up, I knew we were going to win. I could feel something special building.”

Man-of-the-match Rice then gave a wry smirk when pundit Daniel Sturridge asked if he had been dancing in the changing room.

The laughing No41 added: “Yeah, you’re right, it was going off.”



Arsenal fans called out Rice’s “half price” chant throughout his interview.

And thousands congregated outside the Emirates to ensure a memorable night lasted a little while longer.

After leaving the ground, the singing continued on the streets of N5.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Plenty of pubs were rammed with supporters toasting the sweet victory while flares were set off, horns blared and the Gooners went through the repertoire of chants.

Many of them will be making the journey to Budapest at the end of the month to watch their beloved side take on PSG or Bayern Munich in the Champions League final.

Sports.title: Champions League pundit ‘wanted to call Uefa and cancel Arsenal vs Atletico’ to make alternative final
Sports.content:
CHAMPIONS LEAGUE winner Wesley Sneijder wanted Uefa to cancel Arsenal vs Atletico Madrid after watching the first 35 minutes of Tuesday’s Emirates showdown.

The Gunners beat Atletico 1-0 on the night and 2-1 on aggregate to make their first Champions League final for 20 years.





But it did not deliver the entertainment factor like Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain did in the first leg of the other semi last week.

That will resume at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night with PSG leading 5-4.

And many people, including Sneijder, reckon those two teams should be battling it out for European supremacy.

Sneijder, on punditry duty for Arsenal’s win, told Ziggo Sport: “After just 35 minutes, I wanted to call Uefa to cancel the match and declare Bayern Munich vs PSG as the Champions League final. That does not look like a semi.”

The Dutchman, 41, won European football‘s premier silverware with Inter Milan in 2010 as part of a treble masterminded by Jose Mourinho.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

So he knows what it takes to sit at the head of the continent’s top table.

Arsenal and Atletico only managed four shots on target between them but Mikel Arteta will not care a jot.



Bukayo Saka‘s 44th-minute rebound edged the North Londoners closer to a seismic double, with Manchester City slipping up in the Premier League on Monday.

And Sneijder gave Arteta his dues – albeit with a backhanded comment about the Arsenal squad.

He said: “This gentleman [Arteta]… I can’t say it often enough, people. But he really deserves a statue already.

“With this team, it is so impressive to reach the final. Leaving all the other world-class teams behind you, I think that is very impressive.”

Sports.title: Diego Simeone pulled apart from Arsenal rival he worked with for over a DECADE as tensions flare in final moments
Sports.content:
DIEGO SIMEONE had to be pulled apart from an Arsenal rival he worked with for more than a decade.

Tempers boiled over in injury time as the Gunners beat Atletico Madrid.





Bukayo Saka turned home on the rebound just before half-time to give Arsenal the advantage in their Champions League semi-final showdown.

And as the clock ticked towards the full-time whistle, things got heated on and off the pitch.

David Raya was booked for time-wasting before Koke and Gabriel Martinelli locked horns when the ball went out for a throw-in.

But Simeone was right in the thick of it in the technical area, too.

The fiery Atleti boss’ frustrations were clear to see as his dreams of a Champions League title evaporated.

And his mood was not helped when he saw Andrea Berta on the side of the pitch.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Berta spent 12 years at Atletico Madrid from 2013 to 2025 as technical director and then sporting director, with Simeone the manager throughout that spell.

The Italian helped sign the likes of Antoine Griezmann, Jan Oblak, Joao Felix and Rodri while overseeing tremendous success, including two LaLiga titles and the Europa League.



However, he moved to the Emirates last year to replace Edu as sporting director.

But despite watching the majority of the semi-final second leg in the directors’ box, Berta headed down for the final minutes.



So much so that he was spotted just metres from the touchline in his suit in the closing seconds.

Berta – who slapped a Manchester City doctor in 2022 – waved his arms at the referee and tapping his watch, indicating that time should be up and the whistle was due.

But when Simeone spotted his former colleague, he marched over and shoved him.

The fourth official and various backroom staff members from both teams quickly separated the pair.



But Berta did not have to wait long before Arsenal’s place in the Budapest final at the end of May was confirmed – sparking more wild celebrations on the pitch, in the dugout and in the stands.

Sports.title: Sir David Beckham blasts Arsenal referee as Atletico Madrid are denied penalty for bizarre reason
Sports.content:
DAVID BECKHAM hit out at referee Daniel Siebert after Atletico Madrid were controversially denied a penalty against Arsenal.

Arsenal reached their first Champions League final for 20 years after grinding out a 1-0 win over the La Liga side on Tuesday night.





Bukayo Saka‘s first half strike was enough to book a European showdown with either Bayern Munich or PSG.

Atletico offered little in north London but might feel hard done by not to get a penalty after Riccardo Calafiori appeared to stamp on Antoine Griezmann in the area.

Referee Siebert had blown up for a foul on Gabriel by Marc Pubil just moments earlier.

But Beckham argued that Gabriel was never fouled in the first place, which means Atletico should have got the penalty.

Speaking on his Beckham & Friends watchalong show, the Manchester United legend said: “Oh my god. Oh that’s not a foul. That is not a foul.

“This [Calafiori challenge] is! Yep! That wasn’t a foul on Gabriel.”

Actor Tom Hiddleston was a guest star on the show argued that the foul on Griezmann was “the same motion” as the one on Eberechi Eze that wasn’t given in the first leg.

But Beckham replied: “Well, I didn’t think that was a penalty. I don’t think he touched him.”

Atletico may feel aggrieved over the decision but they failed to test Arsenal enough across both legs.

They managed just two shots on target during the second leg, with five efforts overall to Arsenal’s 13.

And the Gunners could have been two up had Viktor Gyokeres converted from close range in what was a poor miss.

The result was enough for Arsenal to secure a historic night as they look ahead to a massive night in Budapest on May 30.



Arsenal star Declan Rice said after the game: “It is chaos [in the dressing room]. I don’t think you can underestimate what we have done in this competition up to this point.

“I think we have every right to celebrate that moment. The most prestigious competition in club football. We are just trying to soak it all in.

“We knew coming into the game what was at stake. If you can’t get up for that, then you can’t get up for any game of football.

“When we went 1-0 up, I knew we were going to win. I could feel something special building.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s first summer transfer exit confirmed as Gunners make £6million loss on flop defender
Sports.content:
ARSENAL defender Jakub Kiwior will join Porto on a permanent deal following his loan spell with the club.

The Polish defender, who Arsenal signed for £21million from then Serie A side Spezia in 2023, will leave the Emirates for a fee of £14.5m.





Kiwior has played 38 times for Porto this season and has proved to be an important part of Francesco Farioli’s title-winning team.

And the two-time European Champions will keep hold of the central-defender.

According to an official statement released by the club on Monday, Porto have triggered the purchase clause for Kiwior.

The club said: “FC Porto has triggered the purchase option included in the loan agreement signed with Arsenal FC and will now definitively hold the sporting registration rights and 100% of the economic rights of Jakub Kiwior for a fixed fee of €17 million (£14.5m), plus a variable component that may reach €5 million (£4.3m) subject to the achievement of certain objectives.



Before noting: “Arsenal FC has retained a fixed amount of €2 million from any future transfer of the player.”

Kiwior will also have a release clause set at £60m.

Porto confirmed the league title on Saturday after beating Alverca 1-0 thanks to a goal by Kiwior’s fellow countryman and centre-back partner Jan Bednarek, formerly of Southampton.

It was the Dragons’ first league title since 2021 as young manager Farioli led them to glory in his first season with the club.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

They also had a shot at a run in the Europa League but were knocked out by in-form Nottingham Forest.

Since the East Midlands side dumped the Portuguese giants out, they have gone on to score 12 goals in three Premier League matches, as well as a 1-0 semi-final first leg victory over Aston Villa.

Meanwhile Kiwior’s former club Arsenal booked a place in the Champions League final on Tuesday night as they beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 on aggregate.

Academy graduate and star man Bukayo Saka notched the winning goal after Jan Oblak parried Trossard’s strike.

Sports.title: More than FOUR MILLION Real Madrid fans sign petition demanding Kylian Mbappe is sold after trip with girlfriend
Sports.content:
KYLIAN MBAPPE is coming under intense fire from Real Madrid fans as tensions in the Spanish capital continue to boil over.

Los Blancos have endured a difficult season which saw new boss Xabi Alonso sacked in January after just months at the helm.





They now sit second in LaLiga, 11 points adrift of fierce rivals Barcelona, who could confirm their league title with a win in El Clasico on Sunday.

And nobody is feeling the heat more than Mbappe, 27, after he came under fire for taking a trip to Sardinia with his new girlfriend, actor Ester Exposito.

The forward was recovering from a hamstring injury last weekend when he took the trip, but with the league out of reach and their Champions League exit coming just weeks earlier, the escape has rubbed fans up the wrong way.

Mbappe’s personal team responded to the backlash with a statement that read: “Part of the criticisms are based on an overinterpretation of elements related to a recovery period strictly supervised by the club”.



“This is not corresponding to the reality of the commitment and the work that Kylian does daily for the good of the team”.

The tensions were only compounded by reports emerging that Mbappe was involved in a confrontation with a member of the club’s coaching team.

The Athletic reported that the French international “spoke angrily in insulting terms” to a member of staff who called him offside during a training game.

The incident is said to have affected dressing room morale and, on top of the position of the club and his holiday controversy, has inspired a strong pushback from fans.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

A supporter-made petition to get Mbappe out of the club is being widely shared on social media, and currently reports to have had over FOUR MILLION signatures.

The description of the petition reads: “Madridistas, make your voice heard.

“If you believe change is needed, don’t stay silent — sign this petition and stand for what you think is best for the club’s future.”

Mbappe is not believed to be facing any disciplinary action from inside the club, with manager Alvaro Arbeloa explaining when asked about Mbappe’s trip that what players did in their free time was none of his business.



But as tensions continue to flare, things could get very ugly if Sunday’s result does not go the way of Madrid.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Lewis-Skelly shines in midfield again as Eze is subbed off early after failing to make an impact
Sports.content:
ARSENAL punched their ticket to the Champions League final with a narrow win over Atletico Madrid at the Emirates.

Bukayo Saka bagged the only goal of the game, converting a rebound just before half-time, and the Gunners withstood a wave of late Atletico pressure to hold on.





The 1-0 win in North London followed last week’s 1-1 draw in Madrid, giving Arsenal a slender 2-1 victory on aggregate.

But it was enough to see them through to their first Champions League final since 2006.

And they will be keeping a close eye on the other semi between Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich on Wednesday.

Here is how SunSport’s Simon Collings rated each individual performance…

DAVID RAYA – 8

Kicking was a bit wayward during the opening 20 minutes, which won’t have helped any nervous Arsenal fans. Swiftly settled down, though, and put in another strong showing. Excellent when coming for crosses. A contender for Arsenal’s Player of the Season.

BEN WHITE – 8

Chose the perfect moment to produce his best performance of the season. His connection with Saka seems to be back, as summed up by a lovely pass midway through the first half that so nearly led to a goal. Defended well, too, and kept Ademola Lookman quiet.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

WILLIAM SALIBA – 9

Just an utter Rolls Royce of a defender, who is so calm at the back. Kept Julian Alvarez in his back pocket and dominated the Atletico striker. Great going forward, too, and it was his pin-point pass that started the move which led to Saka scoring.

GABRIEL – 8

More than anyone, he answered Arteta’s call for Arsenal to play like “beasts”. Produced an absolutely heroic tackle to stop Gianluca Simeone scoring, when he had rounded David Raya and the goal was gaping.



RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 7

Got the nod over Piero Hincapie, presumably because of what he offers in attack – and the Italian got forward whenever he could. Gets the best out of Trossard ahead of him, with the pair having a great understanding.

DECLAN RICE – 8

As the England star so often does on nights like this, he rose to the occasion. Made a vital tackle inside the first 15 minutes when it looked like Gianluca Simeone was certain to score. Utterly tireless in the middle of the park and covered just about every blade of grass at the Emirates.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 9

A surprise starter, but kept his place in midfield after excelling there against Fulham last weekend. Picked up where he left off and so nearly created the opening goal with a ball that went right across the six-yard box. Looked at home on the biggest of stages and completed 44 of his 49 passes.

BUKAYO SAKA – 8

Captain for the night, with Martin Odegaard only fit enough for the bench. Fluffed a tough chance from an early corner – but then opened the scoring by poking home Trossard’s saved shot. Clearly still managing his achilles and so had to come off after 58 minutes.



EBERECHI EZE – 6

One of Arsenal’s quieter attackers and perhaps a victim of Atletico being happy to sit deep. So often the man for the big games, but he could not really get into this one and was off before the hour mark.

LEANDRO TROSSARD – 8

Buzzed around and was really lively, with the Belgian having a decent penalty shout waved away during the first half. Helped create Saka’s goal as it was his shot that was saved into the England star’s path. After being off the pace for weeks, looks back to his best.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 8

Led the line well and you have to say that his hold-up play has come on leaps and bounds over the past week or so. Had a hand in Saka’s goal as it was his cross that eventually found Trossard at the back post. Should have scored himself just after the hour mark, but he fired Hincapie’s cross over the bar.

SUBSTITUTES

PIERO HINCAPIE (for Calafiori, 58mins) – 7

Came on as Calafiori began to tire – and he brought some energy to Arsenal’s left flank. Whipped in a great cross that Gyokeres had to finish.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

NONI MADUEKE (for Saka, 58mins) – 5

Lacks the final ball that Saka has and there is a real drop-off between the two at the moment. Could not make an impact.

MARTIN ODEGAARD (for Eze, 58mins) – 6

Recovered from a knee injury that forced him to miss the last game, and so he was able to make the bench. Into the action instantly and fired a shot from outside the box just over the bar.

MARTIN ZUBIMENDI (for Lewis-Skelly, 73mins) – N/A

GABRIEL MARTINELLI (for Trossard, 83mins) – N/A

Sports.title: Arsenal 1 Atletico Madrid 0 (2-1 agg): Bukayo Saka books Gunners’ place in first Champions League final for 20 years
Sports.content:
THE doubts have been dispelled at the Emirates, banished into thin air.

And now, after a night of determination defined by one moment of defensive brilliance, they are dreaming of the ultimate Double.





Just four matches stand between Mikel Arteta’s men and the greatest season in Arsenal’s long history, 24 days to write the most illustrious chapter of all.

With the fans still revelling in the title consequences of Manchester City’s slip at Everton, the goal from Bukayo Saka’s tap-in on the stroke of half-time proved enough to see off Atletico and take the Gunners to their second Champions League final.



Even more important, though, was Gabriel’s remarkable effort to wrestle Giuliano Simeone off the ball when the Atletico manager’s son had the goal at his mercy at the start of the second period.

Yes, either Harry Kane and Bayern or Kvicha Kvaratskhelia and PSG’s team of all the talents will be formidable foes in Budapest.

Yet there is suddenly a sense of destiny about Arteta and his team.

Especially when a manager who has made the percentage calls all season suddenly rolls the dice, as he did when deploying Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But with Declan Rice outstanding, Viktor Gyokeres not far behind and Gabriel a wall of defiance, Arsenal have the sort of momentum that can carry a side all the way.

The Emirates, which had witnessed collective breakdowns just a few weeks ago as the fans feared a meltdown, has been transformed, too – a bearpit of primal energy.

That is what happens when big calls pay off, when players stand up to the pressure, when desire and heart burn with a solar brightness.

And while he was not the star of the show, for Lewis-Skelly this was a night where it may all change for him as well.

There was more than little surprise when he was named alongside Rice, one of FIVE Englishmen in the starting side.



After all, the youngster has become a bit-part player this season, his lack of positional nous noted by plenty of Gunners fans.

Asking a player who seemed likely to be sent out on loan next season to show discipline and poise against Simeone’s expected enforcers, on only his second career start in the role, felt a gamble from a manager who has been all about control.

When Lewis-Skelly was caught on the ball 15 yards outside his own box by Marcos Llorente, the doubts would have grown.



It was to prove an isolated error on a coming-of-age performance.

And it had to be too, for Arsenal to see off Diego Simeone’s grizzled, attritional and resourceful side, who believed they could salvage the tie until the final whistle..

For all Arsenal’s early possession, it was to little effect despite Gyokeres’ relentless foraging and the first two openings came at the other end.



Fortunately, Julian Alvarez toed the first wide, while Rice came to David Raya’s rescue when he looked to have pushed Antoine Griezmann’s cross straight to Simeone.

Indeed, Arsenal’s only serious effort before they scored seconds before the interval saw Gabriel’s long ranger scudding past the post after Ben White slipped Sako in behind the navy blue defensive line.

The initial energy of the crowd had swiftly been replaced by anxiety although Rice’s rampaging runs were a source of comfort.

Griezmann got away with one when an incautious barge from behind on Leandro Trossard sent him tumbling. It would have been given in Madrid last week.

Not that anyone cared when Arsenal went in front.



Gyokeres, so purposeful throughout, ran onto White’s pass and while the Swede was forced wide, his cross found Trossard.

The Belgian twisted to find space for a shot and while Jan Oblak parried Saka, clearly onside, was on hand to prod over the line.

Suddenly, all altered. Atletico had to score – although quite how Gabriel prevented them from doing so five minutes after the restart was hard to believe.

William Saliba misjudged a simple long ball, teeing up Simeone, who rounded Raya with the goal at his mercy only for Gabriel to wrap arms and legs around the Madrid striker and force the ball behind.



Astonishing, match-winning defending, with Raya down to his left to deny Griezmann soon afterwards.

Now it was about nerve and courage, although had Gyokeres been able to keep his side-footed effort from Piero Hincapie’s cross below the bar, it would have been a whole lot easier.



Lewis-Skelly deserved his standing ovation when he was replaced by Martin Zubimendi, Simeone a frenzied bull on the margins of his technical area, urging his side to find the goal they needed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It would not come. It could not come. Not on this night.

Glory stands before these Gunners. They know what they have to do. They believe they are going to do it.

Footage of Casemiro's wife after Man Utd win says it all as U-turn mooted

Manchester United midfielder Casemiro is expected to depart Old Trafford at the end of the season, with his contract coming to an end

Casemiro's wife Anna Mariana Casemiro applauded Manchester United fans' chants of "One more year, Casemiro". The Brazilian midfielder is expected to leave Old Trafford at the end of the campaign.

‌



The former Real Madrid star had been branded a transfer blunder for several years, with Jamie Carragher famously telling him "leave the football, before the football leaves you." He has now become one of United's most important players just months before his planned departure.

‌



Following United's 3-2 victory over Liverpool at Old Trafford, Matheus Cunha appeared to hint his Brazilian compatriot might reverse his decision to exit the club. The former Wolverhampton Wanderers striker said: "you never know" while discussing Casemiro's future.

One supporter wrote: "Casemiro's wife and children stayed over after the game was done to sing along with the fans. You can tell if she had her way. Casemiro would stayed with us for one more year, see the emotions she's going through."

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka complains on Prime Video seconds after Arsenal reach Champions League final
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka complains on Prime Video seconds after Arsenal reach Champions League final

Bukayo Saka scored the only goal as Arsenal beat Atletico Madrid 1-0 in the Champions League semi-final to book their place in the final in Budapest and joked he wanted to be celebrating with his teamamtes

View 2 Images Arsenal Star Bukayo Saka wanted to celebrated with his team after the final whistle (Image: Prime Video)

Arsenal hero Bukayo Saka playfully complained to Prime Video reporter Gabriel Clarke that his post-match interview was pulling him away from the joyous celebrations after the Gunners knocked out Atletico Madrid in the Champions League semi-finals.

‌



The England star netted the only goal of the night to send Arsenal through to the final in Budapest later this month, where either Bayern Munich or PSG will stand in their way of silverware. The Gunners delivered a composed and professional display to end their 20-year wait for a Champions League final, while the Premier League title is now back in their own hands following Manchester City's draw with Everton.

‌



Arsenal are on the verge of the most extraordinary season in the club's 140-year history, with Saka's strike proving the decisive moment on Tuesday night. The Arsenal winger, who was just four-years-old when Thierry Henry and Co were beaten by Barcelona in the 2006 final, shared a light-hearted exchange with Clarke, making clear he was eager to rejoin his teammates in the celebrations after the final whistle.

‌



When asked what the result meant to the team and the club, he told Amazon Prime Video: "Hey, you're taking me away from the celebrations man! It's so beautiful.

Declan Rice admits Mikel Arteta has been tough on Arsenal star behind the scenes READ MORE :

OPINION John Cross Arsenal showed what they're all about...you'd be crazy to write them off now

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"What it means to us, what it means to the fans. We're all so happy.

"This game is a high pressure game and it means a lot to both sides. We managed to manage [the game] well and take ourselves to the final so we're happy."

When quizzed about the atmosphere at the Emirates, Saka said: "It started before the game when we were arriving on the coaches, I've never seen anything like it.

‌



"They pushed us, and pushed us, and pushed us. They've got their special moment at the end so we're celebrating it together."

View 2 Images Arsenal's matchwinner Bukayo Saka celebrates after beating Atletico Madrid

The strike against Atletico marked Saka's 81st for the club, and when questioned whether there had been a more memorable one, he said: "Maybe. It's definitely up there.

‌



"In those situations I just try to stay alive and sometimes it bounces for you, sometimes it doesn't but you have to be there.

"I was there and it fell for me. I got my goal, so glory to god and we'll go to the final now."

The Gunners have faced mounting expectations to finish the campaign with silverware, having been the outstanding side in the Champions League while controlling the Premier League for much of the season. "There's no way you're going to be in this position and not have pressure," added Saka.

‌



"In the semi-finals, now we're in the final of the Champions League. We're fighting for the Premier League, so how can you not expect people to talk about you and criticise you?

"We have to block it out and focus on getting the job done. We did that and it's another step forward."

Sports.title: Declan Rice admits Mikel Arteta has been tough on Arsenal star behind the scenes
Sports.content:
Declan Rice admits Mikel Arteta has been tough on Arsenal star behind the scenes

Declan Rice had a different partner in midfield against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night in the Champions League semi-final and Mikel Arteta's bold selection paid off for Arsenal

View 2 Images Declan Rice praised Myles Lewis-Skelly post-match (Image: Prime Video)

Declan Rice praised Myles Lewis-Skelly for taking Mikel Arteta's tough love in the right way after the youngster excelled against Atletico Madrid. The Gunners booked their place in the Champions League final with a 1-0 win over Atleti on Tuesday night, with Lewis-Skelly playing in midfield.

‌



The 19-year-old has struggled at times this season, with Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie providing stern competition at left-back. After a breakthrough 2024/25 campaign, Lewis-Skelly has found himself left on the bench regularly this season.

‌



He has started just three games in the Premier League this season, has lost his place in the England squad and even been linked with a move away from north London. But Lewis-Skelly has been given a new lease of life in last two games by moving into midfield.

‌



Having impressed in the position during the 3-0 win over Fulham on the weekend, Arteta decided to start Lewis-Skelly over Martin Zubimendi against Atletico. The move paid off, with the youngster composed alongside Rice as Bukayo Saka's goal sent them into their first Champions League final for 20 years.

Arsenal reach Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Arsenal player ratings vs Atletico as 9/10 star drives them into Champions League final READ MORE :

Rice told Amazon Prime: "We have always known what Myles can do. I remember last year when he played so many games. Last year when he stepped up Real Madrid away at the Bernabeu at 18 - I thought: 'Wow what a player.'

"The manager has been tough on him behind the scenes. He has kept his head down and he has worked so hard. He is in early, gym and works hard. To be thrown in at the deep end and perform how he did is no surprise to me."

‌



Arsenal mustered just two shots on target in the entire match and those came within seconds of each other to conjure their goal, with Saka scoring on the rebound after Leandro Trossard's effort was parried by Jan Oblak.

View 2 Images Declan Rice praised Myles Lewis-Skelly (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

But their remarkable defensive record, which has seen them concede just six times in 14 Champions League games this season, got them over the line, where they will face Paris Saint-Germain or Bayern Munich in Budapest on May 30.

‌



"Where this club has come from over the last few years - things that hurt you as a player," Rice added. "The manager has taken full control. We have kept building - we have kept pushing each other.

"This competition and the Premier League. We have gone full throttle. We have found ourselves in a good position with less than a month to go. Sunday now is a massive one."

Arsenal face West Ham away on Sunday when they will hope to build on Manchester City dropping two points in a 3-3 draw against Everton on Monday night on Merseyside. The Gunners hold a five-point lead over City at the top of the Premier League table and are now aiming for a historic double.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney takes aim at Arsenal celebrations seconds after reaching Champions League final
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney takes aim at Arsenal celebrations seconds after reaching Champions League final

Arsenal made it a famous night at the Emirates as they beat Atletico Madrid 1-0 to reach the Champions League final - and the celebration police were soon out in force

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney hailed Arsenal for their performance - but not their celebrations (Image: Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney accused Arsenal of over-celebrating after they reached only their second Champions League final in the club's history. The Gunners beat Atletico Madrid 1-0 in their semi-final second leg on Tuesday, as Bukayo Saka's first-goal proved the difference at the Emirates.

‌



Mikel Arteta and his players are now off to Budapest, and they were jumping for joy and celebrating with supporters at the Emirates after the final whistle. But Rooney wasn't a fan of the post-match scenes.

‌



The ex-Manchester United star told Prime Video Sport: "They deserve to be in this position but they haven't won it yet. I think the celebrations are a little bit too much. Celebrate when you win!"

‌



Former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger was of a similar opinion. "Over the two legs, there is no doubt that Arsenal were the better team," Wenger began on beIN Sport.

Sports.title: Arsenal showed what they're all about...you'd be crazy to write them off now
Sports.content:
Arsenal showed what they're all about...you'd be crazy to write them off now

ARSENAL 1-0 ATLETICO MADRID (2-1 on aggregate): Arsenal have reached the Champions League final with Bukayo Saka's first-half goal the difference on a historic night in north London

View 3 Images Arsenal's matchwinner Bukayo Saka celebrates after beating Atletico Madrid

Bukayo Saka sank to his knees and looked up to the heavens. This will be remembered as one of the greatest nights in the history of the Emirates.

‌



And when the stadium announcer screamed: “Arsenal through to the Champions League final” the whole place erupted again. Nerves replaced by joy and the dreams of an incredible season which will end in Budapest on May 30.

‌



Arsenal were made to fight, scrap and battle all the way by Atletico Madrid’s dogs of war. But you never expected it to be easy, did you? Mikel Arteta’s heroes deserved it and you have rarely seen celebrations like it as all the players danced, jigged and milked the standing ovation.

‌



My word they deserved it. It was Saka, wearing the armband, who scored the decisive winner on the night to send Arsenal into their first Champions League final in 20 years.

Arsenal player ratings vs Atletico as 9/10 star drives them into Champions League final READ MORE :

Arsenal reach Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid - 5 talking points READ MORE :

But there were so many other heroic displays. Declan Rice covered every blade of grass, Gabriel made an incredible goal-saving tackle and even teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly put in another sensational shift.

Viktor Gyokeres finally looked the player Arsenal thought they were buying when they signed him for £64m last summer. Even Arteta let himself go at the final whistle and was dancing as manically as anyone as the celebrations carried on after the final whistle.

‌



Yes, we had the side show of a scrappy, touchline bust-up as Diego Simeone lost his cool and his temper as Arsenal battled through. But this was Arsenal’s night. The quadruple dream ended in March but they can still win two as they are in pole position in the Premier League title race.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta celebrated wildly after Arsenal's place in the Champions League final was secured

And now they are into the final against Paris Saint Germain or Bayern Munich. Yes, Arsenal may be underdogs against whichever opponent. But do not be crazy enough to write them off because they showed over two legs what they are about. Arteta has built a defiant, determined squad with glory in their sights.

‌



They played so well in the first leg, deserved more and this was a war of attrition at times. But they dug deep and deserved it. With spirit and heart like that, they might just be able to finish off the best season in the history of this club.

They have never won the Champions League before and now have the chance to do something not even Arsene Wenger’s Invincibles achieved.

This generation look fearless. After all the talk of nerves and tension, they really turned on a super show. They started well, Atletico came back but it was Arsenal who were the better team overall on the night.

‌



View 3 Images Martin Odegaard celebrates after the final whistle

The goal came a minute before half time. Rice sent a ball forward, Gyokeres chased it down, held the ball up and pulled it back for Leandro Trossard. It was Trossard’s shot which forced a one-handed save from Atletico keeper Jan Oblak and it was on a plate for Saka to fire home from point blank range.

The place erupted. It was reward for Saka whose return from injury has given Arsenal’s season such a lift. But also for Gyokeres.

‌



Gyokeres scored in the first leg in Madrid, got two against Fulham on Saturday and looks a player transformed with his hold-up play, strength and determination. Finally he looks like the player Arsenal thought they were signing.

The second half was a slog. Gabriel saved William Saliba after a rare mistake. Gyokeres fired over a big chance to make it safe. It was his only misstep all night.

But Arsenal were strong enough, defiant enough and good enough to hold on and stay on course for a historic, unforgettable season.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid issued instant explanation over two penalties after Arsenal heartbreak
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid issued instant explanation over two penalties after Arsenal heartbreak

Arsenal reached the Champions League final after recording a historic win over Atletico Madrid, but there were some VAR scares for the fans

View 3 Images Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori challenged Atletico Madrid attacker Antoine Griezmann in the box (Image: beIN Sports)

Former Champions League referee Mark Clattenburg has shed light on why Atletico Madrid were denied a penalty against Arsenal. During the second half, the Emirates Stadium crowd held their breath when Riccardo Calafiori appeared to bring down Antoine Griezmann inside the box.

‌



The Italian made contact with the Frenchman's calf and many anticipated Diego Simeone's team would be awarded an opportunity to level from 12-yards. A VAR review took place but no penalty was awarded.

‌



It was a huge moment, as the Gunners were able to hold onto their 1-0 lead and reach their first Champions League final since 2006. Before they did, Clattenburg revealed the decision stood because Atletico full-back Marc Pubill had fouled Gabriel Magalhaes moments before Calafiori's challenge.

‌

Speaking on Amazon Prime, the English former official said: "I think what the VAR has looked at is Calafiori's challenge on Grizemann. He believes that's a penalty kick, and replays show it was, but there was a foul just before on Gabriel.

"So they had to check the foul first and he agrees with the referee's analysis of a foul. Therefore, the foul outweighs the penalty kick."

However, the same verdict of no penalty was given, with former Premier League forward Alan Shearer explaining that the level of contact didn't warrant a spot-kick Earlier in the match, Arsenal also believed they might have been awarded a spot-kick when Griezmann appeared to push Leandro Trossard in the back.

Neither referee Daniel Siebert, his assistants nor the VAR deemed there was sufficient contact to justify an Arsenal penalty. At the point of the second penalty appeal involving Calafiori, Arsenal were holding off multiple Atletico attacks.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone pushes Arsenal chief Andrea Berta on touchline as UEFA official rushes in
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone pushes Arsenal chief Andrea Berta on touchline as UEFA official rushes in

Chaos erupted near the end of Arsenal's Champions League semi-final second leg tie against Atletico Madrid, as Diego Simeone appeared to push Gunners chief Andrea Berta

View 2 Images Atletico Madrid head coach Diego Simeone appeared to push Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta on the touchline

Diego Simeone appeared to push Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta near the end of the Gunners' Champions League win against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday.

‌



Atletico manager Simeone cut a disgruntled figure on the touchline as his team tried and failed to find a late leveller at the Emirates Stadium. And the Argentine's frustration boiled over when ex-Atleti chief Berta, who worked alongside Simeone for more than 12 years in Madrid, tried to get the attention of referee Daniel Siebert.

‌



As the clock ticked into the fifth additional minute in stoppage-time, Berta wanted Siebert to blow the full-time whistle, and it's safe to say that Simeone was far from pleased with the Arsenal chief. Indeed, Simeone came charging across from his technical area to confront an animated Berta before pushing him back to the tunnel.

‌



Staff from both teams separated Simeone and Berta before the UEFA fourth official stepped in to calm the situation. Simeone then walked back to his dugout and ushered instructions to his side as they tried to score an equaliser.

Arsenal reach Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Atletico were trailing 2-1 in the tie and 1-0 on the night after Bukayo Saka scored a first-half opener for the Gunners. Saka tapped home from close-range after Leandro Trossard's effort was palmed out by Jan Oblak.

Simeone's side had chances in the second half to level, with Giuliano Simeone and Alexander Sorloth having the best of those, but they were unable to take them and exit the competition at the semi-final stage.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta celebrated wildly after Arsenal's place in the Champions League final was secured

As for Arsenal, it's a first Champions League final in 20 years and the Gunners are set to face the winner of the other semi-final tie between Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest later this month.

Speaking post-match, Declan Rice delivered his verdict on the result and the mood in the Arsenal dressing room after securing a momentous win. "It is chaos [in the dressing room]," Rice told Amazon Prime. "I don't think you can underestimate what we have done in this competition up to this point.

‌



"I think we have every right to celebrate that moment. The most prestigious competition in club football. We are just trying to soak it all in.

"We knew coming into the game what was at stake. If you can't get up for that, then you can't get up for any game of football. When we went 1-0 up, I knew we were going to win. I could feel something special building."

Sports.title: Arsenal reach Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal reach Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 1-0 ATLETICO MADRID: Bukayo Saka's goal enough for the Gunners to book their place in the Champions League final with a 2-1 aggregate win over their Spanish opponents

View 5 Images Bukayo Saka opened the scoring for Arsenal before half-time (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Getty Images)

Arsenal moved into a first Champions League final in 20 years with a narrow but controlled win over Atletico Madrid. The Gunners came into the home leg with the scores level following a 1-1 draw in Madrid last week and got the job done in efficient fashion as they extended their unbeaten run in the competition to 14 games this season.

‌



After a cagey first half which followed the precedent set in the first leg, Arsenal took the lead. Jan Oblak could only parry Leandro Trossard's shot and Bukayo Saka gobbled up the rebound. Those were to prove to be the home side's only two shots on target all night.

‌



Nevertheless, it should have been 2-0 when Piero Hincapie sent in a perfect cross for Viktor Gyokeres, only to see the Arsenal striker side-foot his effort over the bar. In the end, it didn't matter with Atleti lacking firepower - especially after Julian Alvarez and Antoine Griezmann were substituted.

‌



Declan Rice had to be alert to slide in and tackle Giuliano Simeone after David Raya pushed a low cross out into the danger zone early on, while Griezmann stung the palms of Raya in the second half.

But really Raya's goal was rarely seriously threatened, with substitute Alexander Sorloth fluffing their best opening late on. Here are the talking points as the Premier League leaders go through to face either Paris Saint-Germain or Bayern Munich in the final on May 30 in Budapest.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Thierry Henry delivers powerful address after being abused on social media READ MORE :

Arsenal transfer officially confirmed as statement reveals £60m release clause READ MORE :

1. Lewis-Skelly takes his opportunity

Lewis-Skelly was the biggest surprise when Mikel Arteta's team sheet went live. The youngster was rewarded for his performance in central midfield against Fulham on the weekend with another start in place of Martin Zubimendi, in a move that will have pleased Thierry Henry.

"Lewis-Skelly showed that that might be a new position for him in terms of next season," Henry purred on Monday and it seems Arteta may agree. His confidence was clear right from the off as he slotted in alongside Rice and moved with freedom in the fluid system, which sees Riccardo Calafiori come inside from left-back.

It won't have escaped Lewis-Skelly's notice that England boss Thomas Tuchel was in the house to watch. It had seemed that his chances of making the World Cup had faded, with other in front of him at left-back, but Tuchel's words from November will linger in his mind: "The door is always open for guys who perform on a regular and high level." The ovation he got when leaving the pitch in the second half was enormous.

‌



View 5 Images Thomas Tuchel had a lot of English players to watch (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

2. Arsenal unlock the door

The Gunners knew what they would be facing: an extremely well-organised, dogged and determined Atleti team. They knew they would have to be patient to pick the lock and, after a tight and cagey first 44 minutes, their moment came.

Gyokeres ran in behind the defence, coaxed Oblak out of his goal and his deflected cross found its way to Trossard at the back post. The Belgian's shot took a tiny deflection and Oblak could only push it out to Saka, who was alive to the chance of a rebound and showed great poacher instincts to tap in.

‌



View 5 Images Bukayo Saka showed poacher's instincts to score (Image: Alex Pantling/UEFA via Getty Images)

3. VAR staying out of it

As ever, there were plenty of decisions for the video assistant referee to check. And, for once, VAR decided not to send the referee to the pitchside monitor.

In the first half, Trossard went over under pressure from Griezmann but nothing was doing. In the second half, it was Atleti shouting for penalties, but Gabriel's challenge on Simeone was deemed to be fine because he got the ball, while Calafiori did catch Griezmann in the box and was fortunate that the whistle had already gone for a foul on Gabriel.

‌



View 5 Images Referee Daniel Siebert wasn't sent to the screen by the VAR (Image: Vince Mignott/Getty Images)

4. The good and the bad of Gyokeres

The debate about whether Gyokeres is good enough to lead the line for Arsenal will continue, but what he is good at was obvious tonight. The Swedish striker missed a brilliant chance to make it 2-0 from Hincapie's pinpoint cross, giving his critics, who say he only scores against weaker opponents, more ammunition.

But there is no doubt that Arteta will have been delighted by his centre-forward's all-round contribution. His physicality is exactly what is needed against a physical Atletico side. And it was his running in behind which stretched the defence and led to Saka's goal. The former Sporting Lisbon man is nowhere near the finished article, as he showed by blazing another shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but he does offer his side plenty of useful attributes, especially when Kai Havertz is unavailable (again).

‌



View 5 Images Viktor Gyokeres battled hard for his team (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Getty Images)

5. Clash of styles awaits

This could hardly have been any different from the crazy, wide-open first leg between PSG and Bayern last week. Arsenal and Atleti play a very different brand of football, so it was always going to be a clash of styles in the final. And it will be Arsenal who will try and implement their brand of football on the more free-flowing opponents in Hungary on May 30.

Whoever triumphs in Wednesday's second leg, which PSG come into with a 5-4 advantage, will reach the final as favourites. But it would be churlish to rule out Arsenal, who haven't wowed the neutrals but have organisation, grit and sheer willpower in spades.

Sports.title: Momentum is shifting Arsenal's way – it could lead to two trophies
Sports.content:
The final whistle went and the Emirates Stadium exploded. Arsenal made it to the Champions League final. Mikel Arteta ran onto the pitch, colliding with his Arsenal players - who were all jumping in a huddle.

"I've never felt that in a stadium before," said the Arsenal manager afterwards. These streets had never seen scenes like it.

What a difference a few weeks make. After months of being seeped in nervousness - which threatened to destabilise Arsenal's season - the stadium was alive again.

As the teams came out of the tunnel on Tuesday night, they were greeted with a huge Tifo of a fleet of boats - next to the words 'Over Land and Sea'.

Image: Arsenal were welcomed by pyrotechnics and a giant tifo in their Champions League semi-final decider against Atletico Madrid

There was a meaning behind it. It harked back to Arteta's comments in January - after losing to Manchester United - about the need to ignore the nerves and jump on the "fun boat" of the season. Back then, the Emirates was stressed when tasked with big moments - and Arteta called for a different energy as he tried to navigate the waters.

His call has been answered. This time, there was no negative feeling in the tricky moments of a testing semi-final with Atletico Madrid. Every tackle, header, throw-in won was cheered like a goal. For the Arsenal fans in the ground, being unconvincing was alright for a change.

The mood in Arsenal's stadium is not the only thing that has shifted recently. It has been a momentous 24 hours for everyone connected to the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was impressed by his players performance and the atmosphere at the Emirates during their Champions League semi-final against Atletico Madrid.

First, Manchester City dropped points in the Premier League title race to hand the initiative to the Gunners. Then the first Champions League final in a generation was reached. There is fresh, new life in Arteta's Arsenal that even the manager himself recognised it.

"Everybody can feel a shift in energy and a belief in everything," said Arteta when asked about the last 24 hours - and especially the City draw at Everton. "Let's use it in the right way."

The wind is sailing in favour of Arsenal. Things seem to be falling into place at the right time. Not only are the fans back onside but key players are returning from injury just in time for the crunch part of the run-in.

Bukayo Saka seems the obvious example of this, with the Arsenal winger getting two goals and an assist in just over 100 minutes of action in the last few days. Riccardo Calafiori has added steel to the defence, but creativity going forward as well.

Image: Bukayo Saka celebrates the goal that put Arsenal ahead on aggregate against Atletico Madrid

Myles Lewis-Skelly is offering freshness to a midfield that has suffered from a different kind of fuel shortage of late. And there's even Martin Odegaard's return to factor in and Kai Havertz still to come back properly after missing some recent matches.

The team is reacting to these small but multiple boosts. Arsenal are not only greater and stronger in numbers - but in confidence too.

Before the game, Arteta called for his team to be 'beasts' against Atletico Madrid and it came in many forms. Whether it was Declan Rice's goal-saving challenge in the first half, or Gabriel's two interventions in the second half to deny close-range Atleti's efforts.

Image: Arsenal's Declan Rice put in a goal-saving challenge to deny Atleti early on

Leandro Trossard was an underrated star for the Gunners, making 10 ball recoveries - twice as many as the next best player on the pitch - as he was tasked with tracking back to stop Atleti's big threat in Antoine Griezmann.

But perhaps Arsenal's new-found confidence, energy and momentum is best summarised by Viktor Gyokeres. The Arsenal striker hounded Atleti's defenders from start to finish, bringing his team up the pitch but also chasing the opposition defenders relentlessly.

Each run from the Arsenal striker lifted the energy in the ground - so much so that the Arsenal fans even forgave him for missing a second half sitter.

Image: Viktor Gyokeres put in a superb shift for Arsenal

"He's not as flashy as other strikers in the world but he does all the dirty work," said Wayne Rooney after seeing Gyokeres' output. "He played a massive role in Arsenal winning this game."

Just when it matters, Arsenal now do not look like a side with holes in it. They do not look like a team missing a top centre forward, nor one making costly mistakes, nor a one struggling with the final task of getting over the line.

While they may not have the eye-catching glitz and glamour of Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain or Manchester City, they do have a steeliness coming through.

West Ham United

Arsenal Sunday 10th May 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

This was Arsenal's 30th clean sheet of the season in all competitions. It was a defence that was never really stretched across this Champions League semi-final second leg. They have now conceded just seven goals in 14 European matches this season.

That gives them every chance to back up a Premier League title race they are in control of, with a special night in the Budapest final on May 30.

"We have the ability and the conviction to do that for sure," said Arteta about making this a special season. That special season could well end in two trophies in just over three weeks' time.

Your views…

Reaction from the Sky Sports audience in the match blog on Arsenal making the Champions League final:

Vic: Losing that domestic cup final to Man City might be a blessing. Arteta isn't the best manager in the world but he might be the best in what he does soon. The team need that winner's mentality more now and to be able to take chances in games when it comes. They have the potential.

Strats98: Sticking with your coach and letting them develop a squad is paying dividends here and now!! Other clubs should be taking notes…

Simon Freyer: What a performance!! Gyokeres had his best display in an Arsenal shirt. Rice and Gabriel were immense, Lewis-Skelly showed maturity beyond his years. Raya made some strong punches. All for one and everything left on the pitch. Bring on Budapest!!

Sports.title: Saka downs Atletico to send Arsenal into Champions League final
Sports.content:
Arsenal reached the Champions League final for the first time in 20 years as Bukayo Saka's goal clinched a 1-0 win over Atletico Madrid at the Emirates Stadium to complete a 2-1 aggregate victory.

On a momentous night for the club, Saka turned home the decisive goal just before half-time after Leandro Trossard's shot had been parried by Jan Oblak, ensuring that Arsenal will face either Bayern Munich or Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on May 30.

The Gunners, aiming to lift the trophy for the first time in their history having been beaten by Barcelona in their only previous final appearance in 2006, were deserving winners but had to come through another fiercely-contested encounter with Atletico.

Player ratings Arsenal: Raya (8), White (7), Saliba (8), Gabriel (8), Calafiori (7), Lewis-Skelly (7), Rice (9), Eze (7), Saka (8), Gyokeres (8), Trossard (7)



Subs: Madueke (6), Hincapie (7), Odegaard (6), Zubimendi (6), Martinelli (6)



Atletico Madrid: Oblak (6), Pubill (6), Hancko (6), Le Normand (6), Ruggeri (6), Simeone (6), Koke (6), Llorente (6), Lookman (6), Alvarez (6), Griezmann (6)



Subs: Sorloth (6), Molina (6), Cardoso (6), Baena (6), Almada (6)



Player of the Match: Declan Rice

It might have turned out differently had the excellent Declan Rice not made a vital tackle to prevent a certain goal from Giuliano Simeone in the first half. There was another goal-saving challenge on the same Atletico player by Gabriel Magalhaes after half-time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Back Pages team reflects on an incredible Arsenal performance that on the night was lead by captain Bukayo Saka

But Arsenal, dogged in claiming a draw in last week's first leg, produced another outstanding defensive display to limit Atletico's chances, clinching a ninth clean sheet in 14 European games and a 30th in all competitions this season.

They also missed chances to kill the tie at the other end of the pitch.

The tireless Viktor Gyokeres spurned the best of them, firing over the crossbar from substitute Piero Hincapie's low cross when well placed to score in the centre of the box.

In the end, though, Saka's goal proved sufficient, as Arsenal saw out the closing stages in relative comfort before jubilant scenes of celebration which included manager Mikel Arteta sprinting onto the pitch to join his players after the final whistle.

Image: Atletico Madrid's Giuliano Simeone missed a huge chance under pressure from Gabriel Magalhaes

Arsenal will now switch their focus back to the Premier League title race, with West Ham next up on Super Sunday, knowing they will have the chance to finish an epic campaign on an unprecedented high in Budapest at the end of May.

Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich go head-to-head in the other semi-final second leg at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday, following a 5-4 win for Luis Enrique's side in the first leg.

Analysis: A night to savour for Arsenal

The magnitude of the occasion was apparent long before kick-off, when thousands of Arsenal fans lined the streets to welcome the team to the stadium. Their coach was greeted by red flares and a wall of noise as it edged through the crowds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal fans lined the streets to welcome the players to the Emirates Stadium with flares ahead of kick-off against Atletico Madrid

The positivity continued inside the ground, where a huge tifo reading 'over land and sea' was unveiled ahead of kick-off as the Arsenal fans roared their side on from all sides of the arena.

Most had anticipated changes to Arsenal's starting line-up following Saturday's 3-0 win over Fulham. But instead of returning to Martin Zubimendi and Hincapie, for example Arteta stuck with the more technical Myles Lewis-Skelly and Riccardo Calafiori.

Image: Arsenal were welcomed by pyrotechnics and a giant tifo

His selection revealed his intent. This was a team picked to win the game. And those in the stands reciprocated. There was an explosion of celebration when Saka and scored and more followed when, finally, the referee blew the final whistle.

The victory is a historic one for Arsenal, whose defensive brilliance, coupled with the late-season of form of attacking players such as Saka, will make them a formidable foe for either Paris Saint-Germain or Bayern Munich as they go in search of the trophy in Budapest.

Arteta: We made history together

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta in his press conference: "It's an incredible night. We made history again together.

"I cannot be happier or prouder of everyone involved in this club. Outside the stadium was special and unique.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was impressed by his players' performance and the atmosphere at the Emirates Stadium

"The atmosphere the supporters generated, the energy, it made it special. I never felt that in the stadium.

"We put everything. The boys did an incredible job. After 20 years, and for only he second time in our history, we are back in the Champions League final."

Simeone: Arteta has done an incredible job

Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone in his press conference: "If we got knocked out, it's because our opponent deserved to go through.

"They took their big chance in the first half and they deserved to get through. If you ask me how I feel, I feel calm and peaceful.

"I think the team gave absolutely everything in the first leg, we could have won it in the second half but we weren't clinical enough.

Image: Leandro Trossard holds the ball for Arsenal against Atletico Madrid

"We improved a lot in the second half compared to the first half tonight. We had chances and there were things that could have gone our way but didn't.

"I think Mikel Arteta has done an incredible job at Arsenal. He has been trying to get to this point for a long time.

"They have incredible financial power and that's linked to what they are doing. I'm really pleased for them.

"They deserve it. They have been working really hard for many years."

Arsenal's record-breaking season

Arsenal have equalled their club record for most wins in a single season (41 across all competitions), previously winning 41 in the 1970/71 campaign.

Arsenal are now on their longest ever unbeaten run in the European Cup and Champions League (14 games), overtaking their 13-game run between March 2005 and April 2006.

Arsenal kept a clean sheet for the 30th time across all competitions this season, with this their most in a single campaign since 1993/94 (30) and most by a Premier League team since Liverpool in 2021/22 (32).

Arsenal will turn their attention back to the Premier League title race as they take on relegation-threatened West Ham on Sunday May 10, live on Sky Sports with kick-off at 4.30pm.

The 2026 Champions League final takes place on Saturday May 30 at the 67,000-capacity Puskas Arena in Budapest, Hungary. Kick-off is 5pm BST.

Sports.title: MVG dumped out as 'breakthrough talent' Nijman maintains ProTour supremacy
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen's search for a first PDC ProTour win of the season continues after he was dumped out of the Players Championship 14 in Hildesheim in the third round.

The Dutch three-time world champion lost 6-4 to Austria's Mensur Suljovic, who capitalised on taking a 4-1 lead to advance into the last 16 before losing to Tom Bissell in the quarter-finals.

Wessel Nijman became the first player since his compatriot Van Gerwen in 2016 to win five titles in a year after he crushed Max Hopp 8-1 in the final.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Michael Bridge and Chris Murphy debate who is the best Dutch darts player of all time

Nijman scooped the £15,000 top prize for a fifth time in just 12 appearances on the circuit.

The Dutchman punished Hopp busting 61 to lead 1-0, before taking an 88 checkout to double his advantage.

The 25-year-old then won another four legs straight to lead 6-0, including an 84 outshot on the bullseye and whopping 140 checkout in legs five and six respectively, averaging north of 110 two legs from victory.

Although Hopp broke in the seventh leg, it proved a mere consolation for the German, as Nijman broke back before sealing the title with a 15-dart hold.

"It's always good to hold your best game for the final, professed Nijman, who produced his best performance of the day against Hopp with a 104.62 average.

"I'm just happy with the way I'm playing. I played well today, especially in the later stages of the tournament.

"I'm feeling pretty confident in these floor events, and I hope I can play like this on the floor for many more years.

"I don't really care about records, I care more about the form that I'm playing right now. It's always good to have those kinds of records in your bag, but it doesn't give you much more than the form you're in.

"I just want to be in the top 16 and make as many steps as close to number one as possible by the end of the year."

Image: Wessel Nijman continued his Players Championship superiority by claiming his fifth title of the year at Event 14 in Hildesheim

The Dutchman kicked off the event with comfortable wins over Daniel Klose and Jurjen van der Velde, followed by a 6-3 win over Niall Culleton to reach the last 16.

The 25-year-old faced his closest match of the day against Joe Cullen at this stage, triumphing 6-4 with a stellar 102 average - the first of four consecutive ton-plus averages before clinching the title.

Nijman then thumped Krzysztof Ratajski 6-1 with a 102.98 average, before breezing past Danny Noppert 7-2 to reach a remarkable sixth final on the floor this year in just 12 attempts.

Hopp, on the other hand, entered the top ten of the Players Championship rankings after making his first final since 2019.

Sports.title: Sky Sports and Audi launch unique 'Flying Lap' track guide series
Sports.content:
Get closer than ever before to the technical and physical demands of an Formula 1 race circuit in a series combining real-life driving in an Audi RS5 road car with advanced simulation data

Powered by Audi: Karun Chandhok takes to the iconic Miami track in a high-performance Audi, combining real laps with advanced sim data to break down racing lines, braking points, and elite-level performance.

Sky Sports and their official Innovation partner Audi have launched a new series, combining real-world driving with Audi's R26 simulation technology to deliver a storytelling experience from the race track never seen before.

At the heart of Flying Lap is Audi's cutting-edge simulation technology, placing the brand directly into the narrative of performance. By integrating Audi Sim data with Sky Sports' world-class production, the series brings fans closer than ever to the technical and physical demands of the circuit.

Fronted by Sky Sports pundit and former Formula 1 driver Karun Chandhok, each episode sees the driver take to an iconic track in a high-performance Audi road car, delivering a full-throttle lap guide enriched with immersive data visualisation.

As they navigate the circuit, viewers are guided through key sections of the track inside the high-performance all-new Audi RS5 with highlighted hotspots. At pivotal moments, the experience shifts seamlessly into a fully rendered virtual environment - where an Audi R26 F1 car screams to life.

Within this graphical world, Audi's simulation data is used to break down the intricacies of elite performance, from braking zones and racing lines to gear changes, cornering speeds, and overtaking opportunities. The camera moves dynamically around the virtual car - from exterior angles to the driver's cockpit - offering perspectives never possible before.

The format then transitions back to real-world driving, maintaining continuity as the Sky Sports driver progresses through the lap, creating a seamless fusion of physical and digital storytelling.

The first Flying Lap episode takes on Miami, one of the fastest and most technically-demanding circuits in the calendar.

Sports.title: Raducanu withdraws from Italian Open
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu has withdrawn from the Italian Open in Rome due to a post-viral illness.

The British No 1 had been practicing in Rome for the past few days and conducted her media obligations before deciding with her team to withdraw.

She has been absent from the tour since Indian Wells at the start of March, pulling out of tournaments in Miami, Linz and Madrid citing the ongoing effects of a virus she picked up at the beginning of February.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Tim Henman and Martina Navratilova debate if Emma Raducanu needs to commit to a long-term coach and improve her off-court physicality to reach her full potential

Raducanu also opted to sit out Great Britain's Billie Jean King Cup qualifier against Australia, but had been hopeful of playing in Rome.

She had been drawn to face Solana Sierra or a qualifier in the second round on Thursday or Friday but she is yet to play a single match of the clay-court swing.

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis just before her withdrawal, Raducanu was asked about her fitness and health. She said: "It's been a long few weeks since I last competed. I've made good progress, good gains in the last few weeks. I'm feeling really positive about where I'm heading and how I'm playing, what I'm doing on the court each day. I feel motivated and feel good to go. That's a real win for me!"

Image: Coach Andrew Richardson guided Raducanu to the US Open title in 2021

Raducanu spent time training last week in Spain with Andrew Richardson at the Ferrer Tennis Academy near Alicante, where he is based.

Richardson was the coach who was by her side when she famously lifted the US Open title as a qualifier almost five years ago.

She has worked mainly with hitting partner Alexis Canter since the split from Francisco Roig, although she did briefly turn again to Mark Petchey at Indian Wells in March.

Raducanu said: "I got a couple of good weeks of clay preparation in coming here and it was nice to see Andrew again. We've kept on good terms but overall I had a couple of really good weeks in Europe. The European clay is a bit different to the way the clay is back home so I'm feeling good overall."

The Brit has been working under the guidance of childhood coach Jane O'Donoghue and physiotherapist Emma Stewart in Rome as she prepared for her comeback.

"Right now, it's about trying to get up to speed in terms of physically, playing points again. It's very different practising and playing points again, and sets, and playing against the girls who are top level. Seeing where my game is at and trying to react sharply to the ball. So that's what I've been doing here, trying to get my eye in," said the former US Open champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Indian Wells match between Emma Raducanu and Amanda Anisimova

The 23-year-old last played in the third round at Indian Wells on March 8, when she slipped to a 6-1 6-1 defeat against Amanda Anisimova.

Speaking afterwards, Raducanu admitted she felt a lack of power had contributed to her low-key display.

"I need to obviously be aggressive when playing those players, but I think there's still a long way to go to be doing that and I need to use my strengths and probably mix it up a bit more," she said.

Raducanu could still play warm-up event ahead of French Open

Image: Raducanu is in a race to be fit for the French Open

Raducanu could still play on the red dirt in the lead-up to the French Open, which starts on Sunday, May 24 to Sunday, June 7.

The Internationaux de Strasbourg (17-23 May) or Rabat Grand Prix (18-23 May) are her last options ahead of Roland-Garros.
